name: beauty-coupon-tier6
summary: The style change knows five beauty-coupon tiers (HairShop01..05) plus the gender-change coupon. 2026 adds a sixth tier, HairShop06 'Beauty Coupon (Extravagant)', for its grade-6 styles, and HairShop00_TD, a tradable Basic coupon. Widen the per-tier array from 6 to 7 entries so HairShop06 becomes the top tier without colliding with the gender-change slot, and count HairShop00_TD as a Basic coupon. Both are found by name, like the stock five.
status: BUILT 2026-09-23, statically verified. NOT yet exercised: the 2026 client's beauty shop does not speak the 2016 style packets (no 0x1079/0x107D case), so nothing reaches this path until the bridge translates it.
why: Operator, 2026-09-23: coupons go Basic -> Deluxe, and 2026 adds one above; a style whose grade is above your best
coupon fails, otherwise the LOWEST coupon that covers it is used. That is exactly Character.exe's logic:
loader (0x401733)  looks each coupon up BY NAME through 0x402CF0 (item table 0x6ED408) into the words
0x6EC8B0.. = HairShop01..05, 0x6EC8BA = HairShop05 AGAIN (the top bound), 0x6EC8BC =
UniChange01 (gender change).
scan (0x4180B0)    fills a caller buffer of 6 x 14-byte entries {id, key[8], biggest lot, total}: entries
0-4 = tiers 1-5 by id - HairShop01, entry 5 (+0x46) = UniChange01.
style (0x4182B0)   required tier = max(grade of the changed hair/colour/face) - 1 (grade 0 as 1), then the
first entry from there up to top - base that holds a coupon; a gender change needs
UniChange (entry 5) and refuses 0x1286 if the grade changes too.
get-info (0x418840) sends the six {id, total} pairs (0x107F) - tiers 1-5 and UniChange.
HairShop06 is id 30495 = HairShop01 + 5, so grade-6 styles already compute its id; they fail only because
tier index 5 is above the top bound. Raising the top bound ALONE would be wrong: tier index 5 is the
UniChange entry, so a gender-change coupon would pay for Extravagant styles and a HairShop06 would land in the
UniChange slot. So the array grows to 7: tiers 1-6 in entries 0-5, UniChange in entry 6 (+0x54).
STACK ROOM. The style handler's buffer is at ebp-0x164; 7 entries (0x62 B) reach ebp-0x102, into the
0x100-byte log buffer at ebp-0x110. That buffer is written only by the error paths' sprintf, and each of those
has already pushed the entry values it logs (0x418680, 0x41879D) or reads no entry at all - checked. The
get-info handler has the same layout and only logs when the scan failed.
GET-INFO KEEPS ITS SIX PAIRS: its UniChange reads move to entry 6, so the reply is byte-for-byte the stock one
(HairShop06's count is not reported; the 2026 client's beauty UI is a different protocol anyway).
HairShop00_TD (30496) is outside the consecutive range. The loader cave looks it up by name next to
UniChange01; the scan cave maps an item with that id to HairShop01 before the range check, so it fills tier 1
and is consumed like one (the scan keeps the key of the biggest stack per tier; consumption is by key). A
missing row leaves 0xFFFF, which no item carries.
NEEDS in the item table: HairShop06 (the new top bound - if it were missing the bound would read 0xFFFF and
every id above HairShop01 would count as a coupon). The merged ItemInfo has both rows.
